items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Now we rehearsed all week with Ed Sullivan, playing on one song.

ctx.x: He could. What’s that, there’s some story I heard about Gubenko, him calling someone Gubenko.

Well he always called me Gubenko. He calls anybody Pops. Well I’ll tell you. Well I know maybe the story you’re talking about. He always called everybody Pops and he always called me Gubenko. He loved that name. Now we’re doing the Ed Sullivan Show. And this goes, naturally it’s much more of a story than just the Gubenko. We’re doing the Ed Sullivan Show and there was one show that Teddy Wilson couldn’t be on because he had other commitments. So they hired a piano player called Bernie Leighton. White guy.…

Benny’s about ready to walk to the right and he says, “Hey Benny.” Now Benny gets a little curve. He never heard that in rehearsal at all. Now walking off he threw a curve and Ed Sullivan was in left field himself, so you get two guys up there, and he says to Benny, “Benny, who’s in the band?” Because he had to ask to kill some time. And Benny looks over at the band and looks at me first, he tried to say Terry, he tried his best, “Uhh Gubenko.” My mother loved it, my relatives loved it, whoa, what a hit. But then…
